headline: PawServe: AI Symptom Help, Breed Finder & Real Vet Care in one PWA
summary: PawServe consolidates all dog care decisions into a single Progressive Web App, offering AI-powered symptom checks, a detailed breed finder, and a comprehensive vet directory.
details: PawServe is a new full dog-care platform designed to put everything a dog owner needs in one place, from health to training. Built as a Progressive Web App (PWA), it can be installed to a home screen for a native app-like experience.

The platform features a searchable and filterable breed finder, allowing users to explore temperament tags, compatibility, fun facts, price ranges, and adoption availability. This provides in-depth information beyond a simple list.

A key feature is the AI Symptom Help, powered by Google Gemini, which offers guided first-aid responses with severity awareness. This functionality is routed through a secure edge function, ensuring a realistic and safer demo experience.

PawServe also includes a comprehensive vet directory that expands beyond general practice to include specialized rehabilitation services. This covers post-surgery recovery, hydrotherapy, neurological rehab, and senior mobility, addressing real owner needs.
Additional pages provide local usefulness, helping owners find places to train, play, and where dogs are welcome. The data model is structured for future growth into richer search capabilities.

The app was built as a static Vite app on GitHub Pages under tight weekend constraints for a challenge. The focus was on creating a complete, usable dog platform with a live Google AI path, aiming to simplify dog care without juggling multiple tabs.

headline_marked: [[Run three AI models on one local server]] even when VRAM doesn't cover all of them
headline: Run three AI models on one local server even when VRAM doesn't cover all of them
summary: A developer shares a sequential loading strategy to run multiple large language and embedding models on a single workstation with insufficient VRAM for parallel execution, overcoming immediate Out-of-Memory errors.
details: Attempting to load Whisper, bge-m3, and Gemma simultaneously on a local machine with limited VRAM resulted in immediate Out-of-Memory errors. The workstation had enough VRAM for any single model but not for all three running in parallel.

The solution adopted was sequential loading: models are loaded, used, and then unloaded before the next model is needed. This approach avoids parallel execution and is suitable for workloads that do not overlap in time, adding only a few seconds of overhead per task.

For embeddings, bge-m3 was chosen over all-MiniLM-L6-v2 due to its superior cross-lingual matching accuracy for mixed Korean/English documents, despite higher VRAM cost. Whisper's medium model provided sufficient transcription accuracy for 30-minute calls in under two minutes.

Gemma was selected for local image analysis, outperforming LLaVA variants and MiniCPM-V on document-heavy images in informal testing. Its processing time, however, varies significantly with input image resolution, requiring careful testing for latency-sensitive applications.

The sequential loading setup has proven stable over several weeks, eliminating OOM errors and allowing individual models to function reliably. The current focus is on building a pipeline to connect these working pieces into a coherent system for processing various inputs.
